newsitem.title: ICELAND: Eruption under Iceland glacier causes flood risk.
newsitem.headline: Eruption under Iceland glacier causes flood risk.

text.p: A volcanic eruption under a glacier in the south of Iceland smashed through the ice on Wednesday, and geologists told Icelandic television there was a risk of massive flooding and ash contamination.

The eruption, which began on Monday underneath the enormous Vatnajokull glacier in the south of Iceland, penetrated a thick shield of ice and sent a column of ash spewing 15,000 feet (7 kms) into the air.
There are no human settlements near the source of the eruption, but falling ash could cause widespread contamination if weather conditions changed for the worse.

Several major rivers originate near the glacier, where ice is now melting fast, and there is a risk that this could cause flooding on a massive scale to the south, east and north, the television reported.
The eruption has been accompanied by volcanic tremors, some registering over four points on the Richter scale.
